nodes.title: Absolutely integrally closed rings
nodes.statement: A ring A is absolutely integrally closed (aic) when every monic polynomial of positive degree in A[T] has a root in A. For a domain this is equivalent to being integrally closed with algebraically closed fraction field; no domain hypothesis is built into the ring predicate.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity. Schemes and morphisms lie in the qcqs category unless the statement explicitly allows a larger class. Cech diagrams and limits use enhanced categories; equivalences and pullbacks there mean coherent equivalences and homotopy pullbacks.
proofSteps: Induct on degree after factoring off a root to obtain splitting of every nonconstant monic polynomial.
For domains pass to the fraction field and clear denominators; integral roots return to A.
acceptance: The constant polynomial 1 is excluded from the root obligation.

nodes.title: Prime extension in the nondegenerate case
nodes.statement: Let f:V→W be a map of aic valuation domains and p a prime of V. If ker f⊆p and pW≠W, then pW is prime and contracts to p. There is a largest prime q of W contracting to p, and W⊗_V V_p≃W_q, W⊗_V V/p≃W/pW, W⊗_V κ(p)≃W_q/pW_q. The primes pW and q need not coincide.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity. Schemes and morphisms lie in the qcqs category unless the statement explicitly allows a larger class. Cech diagrams and limits use enhanced categories; equivalences and pullbacks there mean coherent equivalences and homotopy pullbacks.
proofSteps: Replace V by V/ker f, which retains p under the kernel-containment hypothesis.
Divisibility of the valuation groups makes pW radical; use total divisibility and properness of pW to prove contraction.
The union of all primes contracting to p is the largest such q. Compare prime spectra of localizations to identify W⊗V_p with W_q; then quotient by p.
acceptance: The second localization uses the largest prime over p, not automatically pW.
For a field V embedded in a positive-rank aic W and p=0, pW=0 while q is the maximal ideal of W.

nodes.title: Universal descent of the valuation split
nodes.statement: If a finitary v-sheaf F has aic-v-excision and cotruncated-compact target, then Spec(V/p)⊔Spec(V_p)→Spec V is of universal F-descent for every aic V.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity. Schemes and morphisms lie in the qcqs category unless the statement explicitly allows a larger class. Cech diagrams and limits use enhanced categories; equivalences and pullbacks there mean coherent equivalences and homotopy pullbacks.
proofSteps: Reduce an arbitrary base change to a map V→W of aic valuation rings.
If pW=W the square is trivial. If p⊊ker(V→W), choose s∈ker minus p: then pW=0, W⊗V_p=0 and W⊗κ(p)=0, leaving the identity square.
When ker f⊆p and pW≠W, use the largest prime q over p to write the base-change square with W_q. Paste the prime-splitting squares for W at pW and for W_q at pW_q; their common localization is W_(pW).
acceptance: All three cases, including p strictly below the kernel, must appear in the proof.

nodes.title: The arc-descent criterion
nodes.statement: Let C be compactly generated by cotruncated objects and F:Sch_qcqs,R^op→C a finitary v-sheaf. The following are equivalent: F is an arc-sheaf; F is excisive for all Milnor squares; F satisfies aic-v-excision.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity. Schemes and morphisms lie in the qcqs category unless the statement explicitly allows a larger class. Cech diagrams and limits use enhanced categories; equivalences and pullbacks there mean coherent equivalences and homotopy pullbacks.
proofSteps: Arc-descent gives splitting descent; unwind the valuation-split Cech nerve to obtain aic-v-excision.

For the converse reduce to affine finitely presented covers over aic V. Use interval induction: rank-one intervals give v-descent, outward extension uses finite-presentation persistence, overlap uses universal aic splitting.
For all Milnor squares reduce by v-descent to domains; the domain base-change square remains Milnor. Surjective Milnor squares are already handled by v-descent.
acceptance: Neither finitariness nor the target condition can be discarded in this proof; the unrestricted result comes from the coherent arc-topos.

nodes.title: Rank-one detection of equivalences
nodes.statement: For finitary arc-sheaves F,G with target compactly generated by cotruncated objects, a natural transformation is an equivalence if and only if it is an equivalence on aic valuation domains of rank at most one. It suffices that each such test admits an aic rank-at-most-one extension on which the map is an equivalence. For a finitary space-valued arc-sheaf whose values are all n-truncated for one fixed finite n, contractibility can be tested on these valuation domains; arbitrary unbounded spaces are not covered by this last assertion.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity. Schemes and morphisms lie in the qcqs category unless the statement explicitly allows a larger class. Cech diagrams and limits use enhanced categories; equivalences and pullbacks there mean coherent equivalences and homotopy pullbacks.
proofSteps: For a space-valued sheaf with a fixed finite truncation bound, use descending induction on that bound: its diagonal fibres have a smaller bound, and the discrete case follows by interval induction as in Lemmas 4.9–4.10.
For C-valued equivalences, map out of compact cotruncated generators and apply the bounded space-valued result to fibres, followed by aic-valuation detection.
For the extension variant, first descend the diagonal and its lower-truncated fibres; then use the resulting Cech descent along the faithful rank-one extension, as in Corollary 4.12.
acceptance: This is a statement about sheaves, not a cover by a scheme all of whose components have rank one.

nodes.title: Étale objects over aic valuations
nodes.statement: Every qcqs separated étale scheme over an aic valuation domain V is a finite disjoint union of principal open subschemes Spec V[1/t]. For rank n, write the specialization chain as 0→1→⋯→n. The category is the full subcategory of Fun(chain^op,FinSet) whose transition maps are injective. Morphisms are all natural transformations. Constructible finite-set sheaves form the full Fun(chain^op,FinSet).
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity. Schemes and morphisms lie in the qcqs category unless the statement explicitly allows a larger class. Cech diagrams and limits use enhanced categories; equivalences and pullbacks there mean coherent equivalences and homotopy pullbacks.
proofSteps: Apply Zariski main theorem and strict henselianity, remove the closed-point components, and induct over the remaining open interval.
For arbitrary rank descend to finite-rank subrings by continuity.
Classify objects by their stalks and generization maps; retain all sheaf morphisms.
acceptance: A rank-n valuation has n+1 points; the fold map V⊔V→V is allowed.

On smooth affines, quasi-coherence kills positive Zariski cohomology. Pass to filtered colimits using the defined finitary extension and the cotangent/exterior-power colimit interfaces.
